Willy’s surgery was only possible because of an incredible team. 🤍 From the weeks of planning to four hours in surgery, this case brought together talented vets, nurses and support staff who all shared one goal: giving Willy the best chance at a happy, pain-free life. What makes this even more special is that it all happened in a donation-funded animal shelter. ❤️ Every piece of equipment, every anaesthetic, every hour spent planning and operating, and every day of recovery is made possible because our community believes that dogs like Willy deserve a second chance. I’m so proud to work alongside such an extraordinary team at AWL. Together, we were able to perform a surgery that had never been done before and give one very special boy the future he deserved. Thank you to everyone who supports AWL—whether you donate, foster, volunteer or simply share our stories. You are changing lives, and Willy is proof of that. 🐾🤍 #vet #vetlife #veterinarian #sheltervet #vetsurgery

The easiest Korean meal I make for guests Samgyeopsal Kimchi Jjim (삼겹살 김치찜) 🧡 Ingredients  500 g (1.1 lb) aged kimchi 1 kg (2.2 lb) pork belly 💙 Directions  1. Add the kimchi and pork belly to a pot. Pour in enough water to just cover the ingredients. 2. Bring to a boil, then reduce to medium heat and simmer for 40–60 minutes. 💡 Tips - Don't use fresh kimchi! This dish only works with well-fermented (aged) kimchi. If you're buying kimchi from the store, look for "aged" or "fermented" on the label. If you can only find regular kimchi, let it ferment at room temperature for about 2 days or in the refrigerator for about 5 days before using it. - If your kimchi is too sour, add 1 tbsp sugar. If it's not sour enough, add 1 tbsp vinegar. - You can use any cut of pork, but fattier cuts work best because the rendered fat adds richness to the broth and kimchi. I recommend pork belly or pork shoulder. - I also added 1 tbsp plum syrup and ½ tbsp doenjang (Korean soybean paste). These are completely optional, but they help reduce any pork odor and add extra umami. Since kimchi is already seasoned with garlic, chili peppers, and other aromatics, you don't need any additional seasoning to make this dish delicious. 🔖 Save this recipe for your next meal  🥰 Like, follow & comment if you enjoyed  .  .  . .  . . #k#koreanfoode#EasyRecipesc#comfortfoodkimchi #samgyupsal
